name: Imran Khan
role: Pakistani cricketer, founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) and Prime Minister of Pakistan (2018-2022); imprisoned since 2023
summary: Khan combines anti-corruption and anti-elite populism with an Islamic welfare-state vision modelled on Medina, expanded poverty programmes (Ehsaas, Sehat Sahulat) and a pro-private-sector growth agenda. He defends Pakistan's blasphemy laws, pursues an independent foreign policy tilted to China and refuses US bases, and has been critical of army interference in politics since his 2022 removal. His remarks on women's dress and the Taliban takeover drew heavy criticism.

sources.usedFor: PTI ideology and 2018 agenda

universal-healthcare.rationale: Government expanded the state-funded Sehat Sahulat health insurance; Khan framed it as a step toward universal coverage, though it is targeted at poorer households.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said tax-avoiding elites should carry more of the adjustment and the manifesto targeted big evaders and a shift to direct taxes, but it also called for a flatter, simpler system; no call for higher rates.

unions-good.rationale: The 2018 manifesto he led promised trade union rights and repeal of repressive labour laws.

cut-welfare.rationale: Launched and expanded Ehsaas and Sehat Sahulat as flagship welfare policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Urged Muslim governments to press Western states to criminalise insults against the Prophet, comparing it to Holocaust-denial laws.

decide-locally.rationale: Manifesto pledged full provincial autonomy, stronger directly funded local governments and devolution.

more-religion-public.rationale: Set the goal of a welfare state on the Medina model, urged clerics to play a pivotal role, and added a Seerat-un-Nabi subject to the syllabus.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In Aug 2021 curriculum launch he said adopting another culture makes people slaves to it, arguing for own cultural identity.

nation-first.rationale: Insisted on an independent foreign policy that benefits Pakistan and refused US demands for bases.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Manifesto called climate change an existential threat; as PM launched the tree drive, cancelled 2,600 MW of coal and set a 60% clean-energy target.

democracy-best.rationale: Called his aim an "Islamic democracy" and contested elections, but in 2021 praised China's party system as having beaten Western democracies on merit.

separate-church-state.rationale: Seeks a modern Islamic republic and a welfare state on the Medina model, with a role for religious scholars.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Invokes Medina state principles and defends blasphemy laws; has not set out a general programme of scripture-based law.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Refused to recognise Israel until Palestinians get their rights, in line with a two-state solution; no statement on a right to a state in itself.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supports Kashmiri self-determination under UN resolutions.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Government stopped approving new coal plants and dropped 2,600 MW of planned coal.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-corruption and attacks on entrenched elites are the core of his politics; at the UN he spoke on elite money laundering.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: His government added Seerat-un-Nabi to the syllabus and introduced the Single National Curriculum, which critics said increased religious content.

separated-powers.rationale: Manifesto sought an independent judiciary, parliamentary scrutiny of the defence budget and devolution.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Welfare-state vision and Ehsaas programme aimed at lifting the poor; stated Medina state looks after the downtrodden.

party-controls-media.rationale: Manifesto promised press freedom and he denied persecuting journalists, though rights groups reported declining media freedom under his government.

death-penalty.rationale: Called for public hanging of rapists and child abusers (Sept 2020); did not specifically address terrorism in the source.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Called for debt relief for developing nations during the pandemic.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Manifesto he led committed to strengthening the nuclear deterrent and missile programme.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Called India's 2019 actions in Kashmir appalling and urged the UN to act; hardened stance after revocation of special status.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: PTI promised to end dependence on foreign aid, though his government took a US$6bn IMF programme.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Described the Chinese party model as unique and Medina as a model, while stressing Western democracy is not the only route.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Manifesto sought civilian oversight of the military and ISI reporting to the PM; in 2023 he described army interference as long-standing reality rather than endorsing it, while having extended Bajwa's tenure as PM.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Sehat Sahulat is publicly funded but delivers cash-free care at empanelled public and private hospitals.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Defended Pakistan's blasphemy laws and opposed changing them; his position on punishing "false religion" is not recorded.

social-market-economy.rationale: Manifesto limits the state to enabling private wealth creation while adding health insurance and poverty programmes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Manifesto committed to modernising the armed forces and strengthening the deterrent.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Manifesto: relations with the US, China, Russia all serve Pakistan; he balanced them and refused US bases.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Presents PTI as the only non-dynastic mainstream party and campaigned against dynastic politics.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: His government accepted the 2019 IMF programme with fiscal consolidation and energy reform.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Said he would "never have agreed" to US military bases and "absolutely not" in June 2021.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Described as calling himself a pacifist and opposing the Iraq War, while approving a military response to Indian attack.

farm-price-support.rationale: Manifesto proposed linking crop prices to input costs and a crop and livestock insurance scheme.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Manifesto committed to strengthen the nuclear deterrent.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Manifesto pledged to ensure women's inheritance and property rights.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Manifesto and UN speech call for a resolution of Kashmir based on self-determination and UN resolutions.

close-ties-china.rationale: Strong supporter of CPEC and closer China ties in manifesto and as PM; called China one of Pakistan's greatest friends.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Ehsaas and Sehat Sahulat target poor households via poverty registries.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Manifesto called for ending tax exemptions that benefit special interests.

notes: Wikipedia reports he has been held in Adiala Jail since 2023 with 2025 sentences in the Al-Qadir Trust and Toshakhana-II cases; he says the cases are political. The original books, full UNGA 2019 text and official manifesto PDF could not be opened, so answers rest on news reports of his statements and a SlideShare copy of the manifesto. His relationship to the army changed: he extended Bajwa in 2019 but blamed the army for his removal. Pre-2022 and post-2022 views on the US (partner vs alleged conspirator) are not used for any answer.
